newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ANZ bank posts sharply higher profit.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ANZ bank posts sharply higher profit.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) reported an 18 percent rise in first half net profit on Wednesday, defying market predictions that tighter margins would see only modest growth in earnings.
Australia's third largest bank announced a net profit for the six months to March 31 of A$615 million (US$470 million), up from A$520 million for the previous corresponding half.
Most of ANZ's overseas operations boosted their contributions to group profits. New Zealand contributed an operating profit of A$77 million, up from A$68 million.
But profits were especially buoyant in ANZ's core Australian markets, where higher fees and business lending growth more than offset tight interest rate margins.
Operating income in Australia rose by almost 35 percent to A$405 million.
The bank also announced that chief executive Don Mercer would retire at the end of the year.
Mercer said the general slowdown in the New Zealand economy had constrained asset growth.
All four of Australia's big banks have been seen as vulnerable to foreign takeover because the government h as barred mergers between the major four banks.
But ANZ chairman Charles Goode said on Wednesday ANZ was big enough and had sufficient growth to continue as a successful and independent bank.
ANZ shares hit a record high of A$8.70 after the results, up 13 cents on Tuesday's close.
